I'm going to go to my first yoga class tonight, purely for flexibility reasons. Any accomplished yoga shitpeople in here who would like to give me some things to avoid (besides fat instructors)?

I generally find I take better to getting negative advice (e.g. don't heel strike when running, don't steer with the wrong part of drop bars) rather than getting tips per se.

I love yoga.

When the instructor gives you the option of doing an easier pose, do it if you need to. Don't manly-man eat that shit. No one cares, no one is watching you. Take the easier pose if you need. In time you'll kick that pose in the dick. Take it easy on your first night.

Don't get self conscious. Again, no one gives a shit about you, no one but the instructor is watching you. So don't convince yourself that they are. It sounds weird, but a lot of people work themselves into showing off or holding poses they really can't, because they worry how they look to the people next to them. Hot or not, they aren't looking. They don't care. Take care of you.

I have low arches on my feet, pretty much flat footed. I regularly felt pain on the underside of my feet when doing warrior poses and the like. Turns out it's just that yoga mats are shit if you have flat feet. If that applies to you, do back-work on the mat, but when you're standing, including sun salutations, do it on the hard floor next to the mat. If you must have something under your flat feet, use a towel.

Ujai breath is metal as fuck. Focus on that shit. Seriously. Breathing, holding, crushing poses by holding them long with staining muscles, breathing through it... Focus on that breathing.

Enjoy. Also stay clear of fats, they have no body control and will often talk/wine through lessons. Luckily snce I've done yoga for years I haven't seen a fat in forever, certainly not at a level higher than intro.

When doing downward dog, don't rest your weight on the heel area of your hands. Even at human weights, it puts strain on your wrists. This is the graphic that taught me what to do: https://s-media-cache-ak0.pinimg.com/736x/72/ed/64/72ed648c08b32c52e67ab85fef162959.jpg

source: Do yoga frequently but not regularly, was having sore wrists, googled.

I am so excited for you! I fucking love yoga so much. I am so far from accomplished but I've been doing it for a while now. I'm not good at negative advice either, but just some stuff (this may seem obvious too):

Wear tight to medium loose clothing. I prefer tight pants and shirt simply so when I go upside down it doesn't fall and flash everyone.

If you fall, no one gives a shit. So go ahead and fall, but make sure you get a blanket under you so you don't break yourself.

Use blocks.

I know up the thread someone said you shouldn't look around during class but I honestly do ONLY to make sure my form is right. I think this is ok. It's best to do this to compare to the teacher when they're not walking around. Feel free to ask the teacher questions though, they should be helpful and nice because 99% of yoga teachers are hippie dippie people and are into helping people.

Bring water.

Rest as often as you need to. You should ideally take what you need away from the class, and that includes using your body in a way that is best for you. If that means you can't hold a pose as long as an instructor wants you to, fine, especially for a beginner. I would suggest really concentrating on your breath and flowing with it as much as you can (you'll understand this better after class).
